claims.text: A symmetry-preserving machine-learning model can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Strong chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys affects phonon scattering and thermal transport.
The machine-learning model will outperform traditional ab initio methods for predicting low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 is an example of a chemically disordered high-entropy alloy.
High-entropy alloys typically occur as single-phase random solid solutions.
Atomic species and positions can be used as inputs to directly predict phonon density of states.
A predicted phonon density of states can indirectly provide an accurate prediction of phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model is trained and validated on a diverse crystalline-material dataset that includes high-entropy alloys.
The model is applicable to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and structures are similar to those represented in its training set.
The model's applicability excludes alloys with phase separation or significant local ordering.
Chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys produces mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations strongly reduce phonon lifetimes.
Euclidean neural networks can be equivariant to three-dimensional rotations, translations, and inversion and thereby capture crystal symmetry.
Symmetry equivariance enables the model to capture the stochastic effects of multi-element disorder.
The model can infer both the distribution of phonon modes and their scattering characteristics.
The model will provide a significant improvement in prediction accuracy and computational speed over conventional ab initio methods.
The model will identify low-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys with roughly 70–80% accuracy on benchmark datasets.
Existing ab initio calculations and empirical correlations struggle to capture chemical disorder and complex phonon dynamics in high-entropy alloys.
Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering can experimentally characterize lattice dynamics in Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20.
